Mixed day steps for tag checks
New staff will learn the order of work

This page covers Companion Animal Travel Desk intake and release checks, and it matters because every carrier, label, and handoff must hold up under pressure. You are part of the ground team that keeps animals moving safely between services, so your pace must stay calm, exact, and respectful even when the counter is busy. Start by confirming the booking file, then match the traveler details to the animal record and the carrier in front of you. If anything is unclear, stop and raise it at once instead of guessing.

For small dogs, check the crate fit with care and keep the animal comfortable while you inspect the door, latch, and ventilation. <<FACT F068>> After that, confirm the tag is secure and that the carrier shows the right route notes. Speak plainly to the traveler, because rushed words create avoidable errors and slow down the line.

For reptiles, the age gate is a safety point that cannot be skipped. <<FACT F078>> Once that check is complete, review the enclosure condition, the closure points, and the handling note before the animal is moved forward. Keep the interaction brief and steady, and never leave the traveler unsure about the next step. The desk must protect welfare first, then maintain smooth flow to the gate team and the loading crew.

When you receive a carrier, use both eyes and both hands. Look for loose fittings, strain on the seams, and signs that the animal is unsettled. If the carrier needs attention, place it aside and call the senior coordinator immediately. If the paperwork is complete, pass the file onward without delay and record the handoff in the station log.

Remember that Aurelia Skyways relies on clear action, careful checks, and steady judgment from the Companion Animal Travel Desk, so the safest choice is the one that leaves no doubt.
